title: feat(app-shell): a module-internal record-preview card for any (object, id) pair (objectui#12029)
body:
Fixes #12029
Clause-②: no

## What this adds

One module-internal component, `RecordPreviewCard`, at `packages/app-shell/src/views/record-preview/RecordPreviewCard.tsx`, with its tests beside it and a `patch` changeset. It takes `objectName`, `recordId` and a data source, and renders a compact card for that pair. This is the A2 child of objectui#2763. Nothing re-exports it from the package entry and it registers no component type: registering it as a type page metadata can reference is B1's step, where it is first consumed.

## Premise check, on `main` `8f8f760f`

- **What the approval surfaces show for a target today.** The inbox's `RecordCell` shows `record_title || formatIdentity(record_id)`: a link when the readability probe allows one, plain text when it does not, and the tombstone or the cause-free label in the two dead-reference cases. `RecordApprovalsPanel` sits on the record page itself, so its target is the page's own record and it draws no target card.
- **An existing compact rendering from `(object, id)`: none.** Read: `LookupField` (its popover is a picker, its chip a label), `RecordDetailView` in `embedded` mode (the whole record page inside a drawer), plugin-dashboard's `RecordDetailDrawer` (draws a row it already holds and reads nothing), the global-search hit cards (server hits, no definition read). What does exist is the record page header's three pieces: `getRecordDisplayName` (the title), `deriveHighlightFields` with `detectStatusField` (which fields), and `HeaderHighlight` (how they are drawn). The card composes those three instead of adding a fourth rendering.
- **`useRecordReadability` cannot be reused as code from app-shell.** It lives in `apps/console` (`pages/system/recordReadability.ts`) and imports `useAdapter` from `@object-ui/app-shell`, so importing it back would be a dependency cycle. The card keeps its RULE instead: an unreadable target says nothing about why, and it shows the inbox's own cause-free sentence, read by its existing key `approvalsInbox.recordUnresolvable` (no new pack key).
- **"Absent, the record is gone" cannot be learned from the card's own read.** `ObjectStackAdapter.findOne` resolves `null` on a 404, and the platform answers a by-id read of a record outside the viewer's row set with that same 404 on purpose. The objectui#8631 ruling forbids telling "deleted" from "not visible" (an existence oracle). So in this card `absent` means the REFERENCE is absent (no object name or no record id): nothing is read and the shared empty-value dash renders. A deletion the platform asserts (an approval's `record_deleted`) stays the caller's to render, as the inbox's tombstone does today.

## The four states, each pinned

| State | When | What renders |
|---|---|---|
| loading | the definition or the record read is in flight | a `role="status"` card with the shared `common.loading` text |
| readable | `findOne` returned the record | the object label, the title, the highlight fields |
| unreadable | no definition, no data source, `findOne` resolved `null`, rejected (refused or failed) or threw | one cause-free card: the same DOM for every one of those causes |
| absent | the pair names no record | the shared `EmptyValue` dash, and zero reads |

## Rules reused, not restated

- **Title:** `getRecordDisplayName` from `@object-ui/core`, the one ADR-0079 ladder the record page's H1 and breadcrumb read.
- **Key fields:** `deriveHighlightFields(def, detectStatusField(def))`, the call the synthesized record page makes for its highlights strip: the object's declared `highlightFields` first, else the same heuristic.
- **Field values:** `HeaderHighlight`, the record page's own strip.
- **Field-level security:** the served row goes through `withoutDeniedFields` before the title and the fields read it, and the `$expand` list is gated by the loaded policy the way `RecordDetailView` gates its own.
- **Host edit session:** the strip runs inside its own read-only `InlineEditProvider`. Without it, a card mounted on a record page would join that page's edit session: the host's draft would be laid over this record's values.

## Data path and cost

- **Definition:** `useMetadataItem('object', name)`, the console's existing hook. A cache hit when the provider already holds the object; otherwise one by-name read that `MetadataProvider` de-duplicates in flight and caches. **N cards of one object share one definition read**, pinned against the real `MetadataProvider`: three cards of one object and one of another make exactly one by-name read per object.
- **Record:** one `findOne` per card, in the record page's request shape: no params, or `$expand` naming only the reference fields the card shows. N cards for N ids are N record reads, not batched; a list surface that renders many cards (B2) should weigh that.
- **Refresh:** `useDataInvalidation` re-reads in place, and the card keeps what it shows until the answer lands.
- **First load:** nothing imports the module, so it moves no first-load bytes.

## Tests and reverse verification

All runs from the worktree root on HEAD `b3fe66cb0` (the type-check ran on the same bytes just before that commit; nothing changed after it).

- `pnpm exec vitest run packages/app-shell/src/views/record-preview/`: `Test Files 1 passed (1)`, `Tests 13 passed (13)`. The pins: absent (four ways a pair can name nothing, zero reads), loading until the read answers, the title by the declared `nameField` over a record that also carries `name`, `$expand` only for a shown reference field, refresh in place on invalidation, one identical unreadable rendering for a `null` read, a refused read, a failed read, a throwing data source and a missing definition (the last with zero record reads), one definition read for N cards under the real `MetadataProvider`, a denied field neither drawn nor expanded, and a host edit session kept out.
- Reverse verification through objectstack `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` in wrap mode: each mutation's anchor had to hit once, the blob had to change, and the restore was proven by the blob hash equal to HEAD's and an empty `git diff HEAD`. The test imports the module by relative path, so no build sits between a mutation and its run.
  - **U, drop the unreadable branch** (`return null` where the unreadable card is returned): `Tests 1 failed | 12 passed`, the unreadable pin. The first attempt was a no-op: its anchor was contained in its own replacement, so the tool refused it and ran nothing. It was redone with an anchor the replacement does not contain.
  - **T, break the title rule** (`String(row.name ?? '')` in place of `getRecordDisplayName`): `Tests 2 failed | 11 passed`, the title pin and the N-cards pin.
  - **I, drop the read-only `InlineEditProvider`** around the strip: `Tests 1 failed | 12 passed`, the host-isolation pin.
  - Expected direction for all three: red. Observed: red.

The built entry declarations do not reach the module: `dist/index.d.ts` and `dist/index.js` have zero hits for it (control: `RecordDetailView` hits `dist/index.d.ts`), and no other emitted file imports it. No locale pack and no export changed, so the pack-parity and `check:readme-exports` gates are not owed.

**Lint is a declared narrowing.** The population is what eslint's own config applies to these files (`--print-config` on the component lists 118 rules, `react-hooks/exhaustive-deps` among them); the file count, 2, is read from `--format json`; and the root config enables no type-aware linting (no `parserOptions.project` or `projectService`), so this diff cannot move any untouched file's verdict. The repo-wide `pnpm lint` is CI's.

## Acceptance notes

- A declared `highlightFields` list longer than four is capped at four by `deriveHighlightFields`' default. The record page's own path hands the declared list on uncapped. Same fields, same order; the card shows the first four.
- The card passes each highlight field's definition label as the label fallback. The record page's synthesized strip passes none. Whether that strip draws an empty label when no translation bundle names the field was not measured here.
- `RecordDetailView` also reads `{ name }` descriptors out of an object's `highlightFields`, which the spec declares as an array of strings. The card reads only through `deriveHighlightFields`, which keeps strings.

## Not measured

- **NOT MEASURED: the full `packages/app-shell/` vitest run.** Started under the shared lock with `--maxWorkers=2` and stopped by me after 23m27s (exit 143, no results printed) because two other agents were queued behind it. Replaced by a declared narrowing: the diff adds only new files that nothing imports, so an existing app-shell test can reach them only by enumerating files on disk. The 21 tests that do were found by grepping the package's tests for `readdirSync`, `globSync`, `readdir(`, `walk(`, `listSourceFiles`, `import.meta.glob`, `fs.promises`, `opendir`, `tinyglobby` and `fdir`, and all of them ran green above. Blind spot: a scan through a helper none of those words names. Repo-wide census tests in other packages are CI's.
- **NOT MEASURED: browser rendering.** No surface mounts the card yet (B1 and B2 will), so there is no console route to drive.
